sections.text_helper: Section 30.7.2 "PKA status register (PKA_SR)" in chapter 30 (Public key accelerator (PKA)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 950.
sections.section_content:
Address offset: 0x04
Reset value: 0x0000 0000
Bits 31:23 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bit 22 CMF: Chaining mode flags
This status bit is only used when CCEN status bit is set in this register.
0: No chaining mode events.
1: Ongoing chaining mode sequence triggered at least one flag status in bits 8 to 14 of this register.
This bit is cleared using CMFC bit in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 21 OPERRF: Operation error flag
0: No event error
1: An illegal or unknown operation has been selected in PKA_CR register
This bit is cleared using OPERRFC bit in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 20 ADDRERRF: Address error flag
0: No address error
1: Address access is out of range (unmapped address)
This bit is cleared using ADDRERRFC bit in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 19 RAMERRF: PKA RAM error flag
0: No PKA RAM access error
1: An AHB access to the PKA RAM occurred while the PKA core was computing and using its
internal RAM (AHB PKA_RAM access are not allowed while PKA operation is in progress).
This bit is cleared using RAMERRFC bit in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 18 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bit 17 PROCENDF: PKA end of operation flag
0: Operation in progress
1: PKA operation is completed. This flag is set when the BUSY bit is deasserted.
Bit 16 BUSY: Busy flag
This bit is set whenever a PKA operation is in progress (START = 1 in PKA_CR). It is automatically
cleared when the computation is complete, making PKA RAM accessible again.
0: No operation is in progress (default)
1: An operation is in progress
When CCEN = 1 PKA sets BUSY bit when it runs a sanity check on a random number that CCB wrote
to the PKA RAM during a chaining sequence (see Section30.3.7).
If PKA is started with a wrong opcode, it stays busy for a couple of cycles, then it aborts automatically
the operation and goes back to ready (BUSY = 0).
Bit 15 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bit 14 RNGERRF: RNG error flag
This read-only chaining mode error flag is active only when CCEN is set in this register.
0: No random number drawn from RNG, or generated ECC private key is NIST compliant.
1: Random number drawn from RNG did not pass NIST “key pair generation by testing candidates”
equivalent algorithm (see FIPS 186-4 annex B.4.2). The last chaining operation must be restarted,
otherwise the selected PKA operation remains unusable.
This bit is cleared when CMFC bit is set in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 13 MDERRF: Mode error flag
This read-only chaining mode error flag is active only when CCEN is set in this register.
0: No mode error
1: The value written in MODE[5:0] of PKA_CR registers is different from the expected value
corresponding to the CCOP mode selected in the CCB peripheral. Refer to Section30.3.7 for
details.
This bit is cleared when CMFC bit is set in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 12 TRZERRF: Trailing zeroes error flag
This read-only chaining mode error flag is active only when CCEN is set in this register.
0: No trailing 0s error
1: Clear-text coming from CPU, or decrypted data coming from SAES does not have the required
trailing 0s.
This bit is cleared when CMFC bit is set in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 11 DATAZF: Data zeroed error flag
This read-only chaining mode error flag is active only when CCEN is set in this register. DATAZF is set
when PKA finds the complete data written to PKA RAM equal to 0, with all the expected 32-bit words
null. This bit is cleared when CMFC bit is set in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 10 INCRERRF: Increment error flag
This read-only chaining mode error flag is active only when CCEN is set in this register.
0: No increment error
1: During the reading or writing of protected parameters from or to the PKA RAM, the application did
not properly incremented the address. Refer to Section30.3.7 for details.
During the read or write of an operand, and before DATAOKF or RNGOKF is set, the INCRERRF flag
stays cleared if the application reads or writes again this operand (starting from the lowest address).
This bit is cleared by setting the CMFC bit in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 9 DATAOKF: Data OK flag
This read-only chaining mode status flag is active only when CCEN is set in this register.
0: Data not OK (if applicable), otherwise no event.
1: Sequential writes or reads to or from the PKA RAM successfully transfered the expected amount
of data from or to SAES. Alternatively, the CPU wrote the correct amount of data in the PKA RAM.
Refer to Section30.3.7 for details.
This bit is cleared when CMFC bit is set in PKA_CLRFR.
Bit 8 RNGOKF: RNG OK flag
This read-only chaining mode status flag is active only when CCEN is set in this register.
0: Random number not OK (if applicable). No event otherwise.
1: Sequential writes to PKA RAM successfully transfered the expected amount of random data from
the RNG. Refer to Section30.3.7 for details.
This bit is cleared when CMFC bit is set in PKA_CLRFR.
Bits 7:3 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bit 2 CCEN: Coupling and chaining mode enable
This bit is set when the application configures the CCB to run coupling and chaining sequences that
perform protected PKA operation using the SAES and (optionally) RNG peripherals.
0: Access to PKA RAM and programming of PKA_CR has no extra limitation.
1: The PKA RAM is write-only until START is set (it is no access then), and the MODE[5:0] value
written in PKA_CR must correspond to the CCOP mode selected in the CCB peripheral. The
application must also follow the coupling and chaining sequences described in Section30.3.7.
Bit 1 LMF: Limited mode flag
This bit is updated when EN bit in PKA_CR is set
0: All values documented in MODE[5:0] bitfield can be used.
1: Only ECDSA verification (MODE[5:0] = 0x26) is supported by the PKA.
Bit 0 INITOK: PKA initialization OK
This bit is asserted when PKA initialization is complete.
0: PKA is not initialized correctly. START bit cannot be set.
1: PKA is initialized correctly and can be used normally.
When RNG is not able to output proper random numbers or when SAES is using the RNG bus,
INITOK remains at 0. If it happens, make sure the RNG peripheral is properly clocked and initialized,
and the SAES peripheral is clocked with BUSY bit cleared in SAES_SR to release the RNG bus,
then enable PKA again.
